scope_note: Residual synthesis after the SV1 public-source audit. It retains one exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold and three reproducible but low-confidence county comparison gaps. The county gaps use 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and an inverse-distance-weighted 20-county benchmark; very wide fit envelopes are retained because Santa Clara County matches poorly. No model converts capacity to consumption, permit value to jobs, or unidentified vendor and community activity to local benefits.

sources.title: County Economic Core Panel, 2001-2024
sources.publisher: U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis and U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics
sources.notes: Repository panel compiled from official annual county real GDP, total employment and average-weekly-wage series. The comparison uses 2013-2020 pre-opening histories and 2024 outcomes; revisions, poor pre-period fit and concurrent county treatments remain limitations.

estimates.label: Annual local public-service-cost break-even threshold

scope.label: APN 224-58-003-00 regular property-tax account spanning the same local taxing jurisdictions

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the verified recurring regular-bill parcel-tax contribution by definition; it is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.

provenance.detail: Verified FY2025-2026 regular parcel bill paid

estimates.confidence_rationale: The threshold identity is exact for the verified regular-bill principal, while actual same-scope marginal public cost is unavailable.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the public-cost level that would offset the latest verified recurring tax contribution without manufacturing a cost or net position.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Project-attributable fire, police, road, utility, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs for the same recipients and fiscal year

derivation.formula: annual marginal local public-service cost at break-even = verified regular parcel property-tax contribution
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed cost.
No supplemental bill, developer contribution, incentive, fee or indirect tax effect is added or netted.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted.

limitations: The regular parcel bill spans several recipients whose marginal costs may differ.
Supplemental bills and the developer-funded substation are outside this recurring threshold.
estimates.notes: No net fiscal result and no actual public-service-cost estimate; this is only a same-scope break-even threshold.

estimates.label: Modeled county real GDP comparison gap

period.label: 2024 Santa Clara County outcome relative to a mechanically matched benchmark; SV1 opening year 2021

scope.label: NTT SV1 and Santa Clara County

interval.interpretation: The envelope is plus or minus twice the 2013-2020 pre-period RMSE. It is fit sensitivity, not statistical confidence.

parameters.name: comparison_2024_value
parameters.transformation: Subtracted from host and used as denominator

estimates.confidence_rationale: The reproducible benchmark fits Santa Clara County poorly and cannot isolate SV1 from the county's technology economy, prior data centers or concurrent investments.
estimates.decision_relevance: Shows 2024 GDP divergence from a transparent comparison benchmark without assigning it to SV1.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: A credible causal design with treatment isolation, adequate pre-fit, placebos, spillover rules and robustness checks

assumptions: Matching uses 2013-2020 log level, average log growth and growth volatility.
Study counties are excluded from the donor pool.
The 2021 opening is not assumed to be first county exposure or an isolated treatment date.

limitations: Pre-period fit is poor and the envelope is extremely wide.
Santa Clara County contains prior data centers and concurrent technology investments.
Fit sensitivity is not statistical confidence.
estimates.notes: Descriptive benchmark gap only; no causal attribution.
